name: APT29
description: Russian SVR espionage group. Responsible for the SolarWinds 2020 attack (30,000+ organizations compromised).

overview: APT29 is a Russian state-sponsored cyber-espionage group operating on behalf of the SVR (Foreign Intelligence Service of the Russian Federation). Public reporting places initial observed activity around 2008, giving the group more than 17 years of continuous operation. Its focus is strategic intelligence collection: foreign ministries, national governments, defence and aerospace supply chains, technology providers, and think tanks that inform Western policy toward Russia.

The group is one of the most heavily aliased actors in threat intelligence. CrowdStrike tracks it as Cozy Bear; Microsoft as Midnight Blizzard (formerly Nobelium); F-Secure/WithSecure branded the pre-2016 activity as The Dukes; FireEye tracked HAMMERTOSS operators as APT29 in 2015. During the SolarWinds investigation Mandiant coined UNC2452 and Volexity used Dark Halo, both later folded into APT29 in a formal Mandiant attribution note in April 2022.

APT29's tradecraft is characterised by extreme operational discipline, patient long-term access and a preference for stealthy, minimalist implants over commodity tooling. In the 2010s the group operated Windows implants (MiniDuke, CosmicDuke, HAMMERTOSS, SEADUKE) with elaborate C2 channels through Twitter, GitHub Gists and steganographic images. Since the SolarWinds compromise the group has re-tooled toward cloud-native tradecraft: password spraying, token theft, malicious OAuth application consent, Golden SAML, MFA-device registration and long-lived residency inside Microsoft 365 tenants.

APT29 was formally attributed to the SVR by the US, UK, Canada, EU and other allies on 15 April 2021 following the SolarWinds compromise, which reached roughly 18,000 SolarWinds Orion customers and gave the group hands-on-keyboard access to at least nine US federal agencies and about 100 private-sector organisations. In 2023-2024 the group re-emerged as Midnight Blizzard, compromising the corporate M365 tenants of HP Enterprise (May 2023) and Microsoft (November 2023, disclosed January 2024), stealing Microsoft source code and executive email, and later abusing TeamViewer's corporate IT environment in June 2024. Parallel spear-phishing operations against European political parties and diplomatic missions (WINELOADER, February 2024) confirm APT29 remains one of the most active Russian espionage threats.

name: APT28
description: Russian GRU specialized in geopolitical espionage operations and disinformation campaigns.

overview: APT28 is a Russian state-sponsored cyber-espionage group publicly attributed to the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU), and specifically to Military Unit 26165 (the 85th Main Special Service Centre, or GTsSS). Multiple governments and vendors track the same cluster under different cryptonyms: MITRE ATT&CK catalogues it as APT28 (G0007) with the aliases Fancy Bear (CrowdStrike), Sofacy / Sednit (Kaspersky, ESET), STRONTIUM and later Forest Blizzard (Microsoft), Pawn Storm (Trend Micro) and TG-4127 (SecureWorks).

Public reporting places APT28's first documented activity around 2004-2007, with Mandiant, ESET and Kaspersky consolidating early telemetry into a single actor cluster between 2014 and 2016. The July 2018 US Department of Justice indictment of twelve GRU officers for the 2016 US election intrusions, and the October 2018 indictment of seven additional GRU officers for the WADA, OPCW and Westinghouse operations, moved the attribution from vendor consensus to a formal government charging document naming individual Unit 26165 personnel and their Moscow office at 20 Komsomolskiy Prospekt.

APT28's mandate is strategic military and political intelligence in service of the Russian General Staff: NATO members and partners, defence and aerospace contractors, ministries of foreign affairs, election-related infrastructure, international sports and doping bodies perceived as hostile to Russian interests, and â from 2014 onward â Ukrainian military, government and critical-infrastructure targets. Unlike its FSB counterparts (Turla, Gamaredon) or its GRU sibling Sandworm (Unit 74455), APT28 is primarily a collection-oriented actor with a well-documented sideline in hack-and-leak information operations (DCLeaks, Guccifer 2.0, Fancy Bears' Hack Team).

Since 2022 the group has kept up a very high operational tempo against Ukraine and NATO allies: exploitation of Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2023-23397) and Windows Print Spooler (CVE-2022-38028, via the GooseEgg post-compromise tool) to steal NTLM credentials, mass exploitation of webmail servers under ESET's Operation RoundPress cluster (Roundcube, Horde, MDaemon, Zimbra XSS chains), and continued abuse of Cisco IOS routers under the JAGUAR TOOTH implant flagged by NCSC UK, CISA, FBI and NSA. In September 2024 the CISA-led 'Russian GRU Unit 26165' advisory (AA24-249A) reiterated APT28's ongoing global targeting of logistics and technology companies supporting Ukraine.

attribution.text: Attributed to Russia's GRU, Military Unit 26165 (85th GTsSS). Attribution has been made by the US Department of Justice through two indictments naming individual GRU officers (July 2018 and October 2018), by the US Department of the Treasury (OFAC sanctions), by the UK NCSC, by a joint NCSC/CISA/FBI/NSA advisory in April 2023, and reinforced by Microsoft, Mandiant, CrowdStrike, ESET, Kaspersky and MITRE ATT&CK.

name: Lazarus Group
description: Prolific North Korean group specializing in massive financial theft and destructive attacks.

overview: Lazarus Group is a North Korean state-sponsored threat actor active since at least 2009 and, by every public measure, the most prolific state cyber operator on the planet. MITRE ATT&CK tracks the cluster as G0032; the US Department of Justice's 2018 and 2021 indictments place it inside the Democratic People's Republic of Korea's Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) and its subordinate Bureau 121. Microsoft renamed the cluster Diamond Sleet under its 2023 taxonomy; older CISA advisories use HIDDEN COBRA; Google's TAG/Mandiant use APT38 for the financially motivated sub-cluster and TEMP.Hermit for the espionage half.

Mandiant's public mapping of DPRK groups to government splits the RGB's cyber arm into three co-located but distinct actors: Lazarus (broad espionage and destructive attacks), APT38 (bank-heist and cryptocurrency theft, the crew behind Bangladesh Bank and the SWIFT campaign) and Andariel/Silent Chollima (South Korea-focused espionage and destructive attacks). BlueNoroff â sometimes rendered as APT38's crypto-focused sub-team â is tracked separately by Kaspersky and Microsoft's Sapphire Sleet. In practice these clusters share malware families, infrastructure staging, and personnel; public advisories therefore switch between speaking of a monolithic "Lazarus" umbrella and of individual sub-teams depending on the operation.

The group's mandate is dual. On one side, strategic intelligence and destructive attacks that serve DPRK regime priorities: the 2014 Sony Pictures destructive intrusion punishing a film that mocked Kim Jong Un, the 2017 WannaCry worm, the sustained Operation Dream Job LinkedIn-based targeting of aerospace, defence and cryptocurrency staff, and (in 2026) the burning of a Windows AFD.sys kernel zero-day on a single defector-adjacent target. On the other, revenue generation for a sanctions-choked state: the 2016 Bangladesh Bank $81M SWIFT theft, sustained ATM cash-out fraud (FASTCash), the 2022 $625M Ronin bridge exploit, the 2023 3CX and JumpCloud supply-chain compromises, and the 2025 $1.5B Bybit heist â the largest cryptocurrency theft in history.

Chainalysis and the FBI conclude that DPRK-linked actors â Lazarus and its sub-clusters chief among them â stole roughly $1.34B in 2024 and, after Bybit alone, more than $1.5B in the first quarter of 2025. Since 2017 Elliptic and TRM Labs put cumulative DPRK cryptocurrency theft at north of $6B. The financial arm's proceeds are believed to fund the DPRK's weapons programmes; the US, UK, Japan and South Korea have imposed layered sanctions on individual operators, front companies and mixer services (Blender.io, Tornado Cash) linked to the group.

attribution.text: Attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) of the DPRK, and specifically to Unit 121 (Bureau 121) and its subordinate task groups. Attribution has been made by the US Department of Justice (2018 Park Jin Hyok indictment; 2021 indictment of Jon Chang Hyok, Kim Il and Park Jin Hyok), the US Department of the Treasury (SDN designations of the group and of Bureau 121-affiliated Chinyong front companies), CISA, the UK NCSC, and reinforced by Mandiant, Microsoft, Kaspersky, ESET and Symantec.

origin.text: First observed activity dates to at least 2009 (Operation Troy / DarkSeoul wiper campaigns against South Korean media and financial targets). MITRE, Kaspersky and Mandiant all place the origin of the cluster in the same 2007-2009 window, with continuous evolution through Operation Blockbuster (Sony, 2014), the SWIFT heist wave (2015-2016) and every subsequent DPRK financially-motivated campaign.

Chainalysis, Elliptic and TRM Labs concur that proceeds fund DPRK's weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes.

notableOperations.summary: Long-running social-engineering campaign impersonating recruiters at Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Airbus, Google, Coinbase and Meta to lure aerospace, defence and cryptocurrency staff into opening trojanised technical assessments or PDF job briefs. name: APT41
description: Unique APT with dual mission: state espionage and financial cybercrime.

overview: APT41 is a Chinese state-nexus cyber-espionage cluster with the industry's most unusual mandate: it runs strategic intelligence collection on behalf of the People's Republic of China while, in parallel, carrying out financially motivated intrusions against the video-game industry. Mandiant's 2019 'Double Dragon' report â still the canonical reference â dates confirmed activity to at least 2012 and treats the espionage and cyber-crime halves as concurrent, not sequential.

The group is one of the most heavily aliased actors in threat intelligence. MITRE ATT&CK's canonical listing (G0096) enumerates APT41 / Wicked Panda / Brass Typhoon / BARIUM. CrowdStrike labels the cluster Wicked Panda; Microsoft's old and new taxonomies are BARIUM and Brass Typhoon; Kaspersky and ESET research the closely overlapping Winnti Group; Trend Micro tracks two sub-clusters as Earth Baku and Earth Longzhi; and in July 2026 Google Threat Intelligence Group added SPIRE CASTLE as its own cryptonym under a new naming scheme. This ficha treats those names as aliases for the same cluster.

Formal attribution comes from the September 2020 US Department of Justice unsealing of three indictments against seven defendants â five Chinese nationals (Zhang Haoran, Tan Dailin, Jiang Lizhi, Qian Chuan, Fu Qiang) and two Malaysian nationals â several of whom worked from Chengdu 404 Network Technology, a nominal defensive cybersecurity firm that in practice served as an APT41 front company. The FBI added the five Chinese defendants to its Cyber Most Wanted list.

APT41's tempo has not slowed since the indictment. In 2020 the group ran a global 75+-victim campaign exploiting Citrix (CVE-2019-19781), Cisco (CVE-2019-1653) and Zoho ManageEngine (CVE-2020-10189) within hours of PoC release. In 2021-2022 it compromised at least six US state government networks by chaining a USAHerds zero-day (CVE-2021-44207) with Log4Shell. In 2023-2024 Mandiant and GTIG tracked a sustained DUSTPAN/DUSTTRAP campaign against global shipping, media, technology and automotive targets across Italy, Spain, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey and the UK. In May 2025 GTIG disclosed TOUGHPROGRESS, an APT41 backdoor that uses Google Calendar events as its command-and-control channel.

attribution.text: Chinese state-nexus cluster attributed by the US Department of Justice, FBI and multiple vendors. Several members operated from Chengdu 404 Network Technology Company (a defensive-cybersecurity front); the group is assessed to conduct espionage under state tasking while side-lining financially motivated intrusions against the gaming industry.

name: FIN7
attribution: Russia / Ukraine — financial criminal syndicate (Combi Security front)
description: Criminal group specialized in card data theft and ransomware.

overview: FIN7 is a financially motivated cybercrime cluster of Russian-speaking Eastern European operators, active since at least 2013, and one of the longest-running e-crime brands in the industry. MITRE ATT&CK's canonical G0046 aggregates the aliases used by Mandiant/FireEye (FIN7), CrowdStrike (Carbon Spider), IBM X-Force (ITG14), Secureworks (GOLD NIAGARA), Symantec/Broadcom (Coreid), Microsoft (ELBRUS, then Sangria Tempest), and Google Threat Intelligence Group's post-2026 scheme (WILD COMET). Public reporting also refers to the group under its earliest Kaspersky/Group-IB names Carbanak and Anunak.

The group's first arc, 2013-2018, was built around the Carbanak/Anunak backdoor and industrial-scale POS malware. Kaspersky's 2015 'Great Bank Robbery' report and Group-IB's 2014 Anunak paper documented up to $1 billion in losses from ~100 banks and payment institutions across ~30 countries. From 2015, the group pivoted to US restaurant, retail and hospitality chains â Chipotle, Chili's, Red Robin, Arby's, Jason's Deli and Burgerville among the disclosed victims â stealing over 20 million payment-card records from 6,500+ POS terminals at 3,600+ locations across all 50 states.

FIN7 organised its recruitment through a front company named Combi Security, claiming to be a penetration-testing firm headquartered in Russia and Israel. The US Department of Justice unsealed indictments in August 2018 against three Ukrainian nationals â Dmytro Fedorov, Fedir Hladyr and Andrii Kolpakov â arrested in Poland, Germany and Spain between January and June 2018. A fourth, Denys Iarmak, was arrested in Bangkok in 2019. Hladyr (2021, 10 years), Kolpakov (2021, 7 years) and Iarmak (2022, 5 years) were sentenced in the Western District of Washington. FIN7 continued to operate through and after the arrests.

From 2020 onwards the group shifted to Big Game Hunting. Public research from Mandiant, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne and Symantec links FIN7 to the development of the DarkSide RaaS (launched November 2020, tied to the May 2021 Colonial Pipeline attack), its BlackMatter successor (July-November 2021), and to affiliate roles for REvil, Maze, Ryuk, Conti, ALPHV/BlackCat, Clop and Black Basta. FIN7 also built and sold the AvNeutralizer/AuKill EDR-killer, mailed BadUSB drives to US defence, transport and insurance firms (FBI PIN, January 2022), and continues to run large-scale malvertising and MSIX-App-Installer campaigns delivering NetSupport RAT, DICELOADER (Lizar) and, in 2025, the Anubis Python backdoor.

attribution.text: Financially motivated Russian-speaking cybercrime group. Attribution is corroborated by the US Department of Justice (2018 indictment against Combi Security operatives), MITRE ATT&CK G0046, Mandiant, CrowdStrike, Microsoft, Symantec, Kaspersky and Group-IB. No state sponsor is publicly alleged.

name: Sandworm
description: The most destructive APT in history. Specialized in critical infrastructure attacks.

overview: Sandworm Team is the cyber warfare unit of Russia's Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (GRU), specifically Unit 74455 of the Main Center for Special Technologies (GTsST), headquartered at 22 Kirova Street in Khimki (the so-called 'Tower'). The unit was publicly identified in the October 2020 U.S. Department of Justice indictment of six GRU officers and, since 2024, has been tracked by Mandiant/Google under the graduated designator APT44. It is the same cluster the cybersecurity community has variously labeled Voodoo Bear (CrowdStrike), IRIDIUM/Seashell Blizzard (Microsoft), TeleBots (ESET) and ELECTRUM (Dragos).

Sandworm is widely regarded as the most destructive nation-state actor observed to date. Where other Russian services (SVR/APT29, FSB/Turla) largely pursue clandestine espionage, Unit 74455's mission is disruptive and destructive effect in support of Russian military and geostrategic objectives. Its operators pioneered the only two confirmed cyberattacks in history to cause power outages in an electrical grid (Ukraine 2015 and 2016), engineered the NotPetya worm of June 2017 that the White House and multiple governments have called the most damaging cyberattack ever recorded, and have used the Ukraine war as an ongoing laboratory for wiper malware and ICS-specific payloads.

The group's technical repertoire spans conventional espionage tooling (BlackEnergy, GreyEnergy, Exaramel, Kapeka backdoors) and industrial-control-system-aware payloads (Industroyer/CrashOverride, Industroyer2), together with an expanding family of wipers (KillDisk, NotPetya, Olympic Destroyer, CaddyWiper, HermeticWiper via related clusters, AcidRain, SwiftSlicer, RoarBAT). Sandworm has also demonstrated firmware-level and edge-device operations through the VPNFilter and Cyclops Blink botnets, backdoored Android applications targeting the Ukrainian military, and information-operations fronts such as the 'Solntsepyok' hacktivist persona used to claim the December 2023 Kyivstar telecom outage.

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Sandworm has run continuous, parallel operations against Ukrainian critical infrastructure and against NATO, EU and Ukraine-support networks, and has been linked by Mandiant, CISA and the FBI to spillover operations against Western critical infrastructure including the April 2024 Muleshoe (Texas) water tower incident. Its tempo and willingness to accept collateral damage make Sandworm the benchmark for hybrid-war-era ICS threats.

attribution.text: Sandworm is Unit 74455 of the Russian GRU's Main Center for Special Technologies (GTsST, military unit 74455). U.S. DoJ named six named GRU officers of the unit in the October 2020 indictment; Mandiant redesignated the cluster APT44 in April 2024.

origin.text: First observed activity is tracked by MITRE from at least 2009; the name 'Sandworm' was coined by iSIGHT Partners in 2014 after references to Frank Herbert's Dune were found in the group's command-and-control infrastructure exploiting CVE-2014-4114.

mandate.text: Sandworm conducts disruptive and destructive cyber operations, information operations, and ICS-focused attacks in support of GRU military and geostrategic objectives, with a persistent emphasis on Ukraine and, since 2022, on NATO and Western critical-infrastructure targets.

notableOperations.name: Ukraine 2015 Power Grid Blackout (BlackEnergy3 / KillDisk)
notableOperations.summary: On 23 December 2015 Sandworm operators used spearphishing with BlackEnergy3 to pivot into three Ukrainian regional electricity distribution companies (Prykarpattyaoblenergo, Kyivoblenergo, Chernivtsioblenergo), remotely opened breakers and deployed KillDisk to erase workstations and serial-to-Ethernet converters, cutting power to ~225,000 customers. It is the first publicly confirmed cyber-induced power outage.

sources.title: IR-ALERT-H-16-056-01: Cyber-Attack Against Ukrainian Critical Infrastructure

notableOperations.name: Ukraine 2016 Kyiv Blackout (Industroyer / CrashOverride)
notableOperations.summary: On 17 December 2016 Sandworm cut power to Kyiv's Pivnichna substation for about an hour using Industroyer/CrashOverride, the first malware framework built to speak native ICS protocols (IEC-101, IEC-104, IEC 61850, OPC DA) and to interact with electric-grid protection equipment autonomously. ESET, Dragos and later the DoJ attributed the malware to Sandworm.

sources.title: Industroyer: Biggest threat to industrial control systems since Stuxnet

notableOperations.name: NotPetya
notableOperations.summary: On 27 June 2017 Sandworm compromised the update channel of Ukrainian tax-accounting software M.E.Doc to push NotPetya, a self-propagating wiper masquerading as ransomware that used EternalBlue, EternalRomance and Mimikatz-derived credential theft. NotPetya destroyed data at Maersk, Merck, FedEx/TNT, Mondelez, Saint-Gobain and hundreds of others, with damages estimated by the White House at over USD 10 billion. Attributed to Unit 74455 by the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Denmark.

notableOperations.name: Olympic Destroyer (PyeongChang 2018)
notableOperations.summary: During the opening ceremony of the PyeongChang Winter Olympics on 9 February 2018, Sandworm deployed Olympic Destroyer, a wiper crafted with false-flag artifacts pointing at Lazarus Group. It disabled Wi-Fi, ticketing, RFID gates and the official site. False flags were unpicked by Kaspersky and Talos; the DoJ 2020 indictment named GRU Unit 74455 officers for the operation.

notableOperations.name: VPNFilter
notableOperations.summary: A modular multi-stage router and NAS implant discovered by Cisco Talos in May 2018 that infected over 500,000 SOHO devices (Linksys, MikroTik, Netgear, TP-Link, QNAP) across 54 countries. The FBI seized the toknowall[.]com sinkhole domain; Talos and MITRE attribute VPNFilter to Sandworm (with links some vendors also tie to APT28-shared infrastructure). Its capabilities included traffic sniffing, credential capture, Modbus scanning and destructive 'brick' commands.

notableOperations.name: AcidRain / Viasat KA-SAT Modem Wiper
notableOperations.summary: One hour before Russia's 24 February 2022 invasion, an AcidRain wiper attack against Viasat's KA-SAT SurfBeam2 modems cut satellite broadband to tens of thousands of European customers and disabled remote monitoring of ~5,800 Enercon wind turbines in Germany. SentinelLabs found developmental overlap with VPNFilter's 'dstr' plugin, and the EU, UK and US formally attributed the operation to the Russian government (later folded by Mandiant into APT44).

notableOperations.name: Industroyer2 + CaddyWiper (Ukraine, April 2022)
notableOperations.summary: In April 2022 Sandworm attempted to blackout a Ukrainian regional electricity provider using Industroyer2 (a hardcoded IEC-104 evolution of the 2016 framework) alongside CaddyWiper, ORCSHRED, SOLOSHRED and AWFULSHRED wipers targeting Windows, Linux and Solaris. CERT-UA and ESET disrupted the operation before impact; CISA and Nozomi Networks published detailed IEC-104 payload analyses.

notableOperations.name: Kyivstar Outage (Solntsepyok Persona) and Ukraine Wiper Wave
notableOperations.summary: On 12 December 2023 the Russian-military-linked 'Solntsepyok' hacktivist front claimed a destructive attack that took down Kyivstar - Ukraine's largest mobile operator, serving ~24 million subscribers - for several days; Ukraine's SBU and Mandiant/Google tied Solntsepyok to Sandworm/APT44 with operators reportedly resident on the network for months. In parallel, CERT-UA and ESET documented continued wiper deployments (SwiftSlicer, RoarBAT, NikoWiper) and CISA/FBI/NSA (AA24-249A, Sept 2024) exposed Unit 74455 operations against US and global critical infrastructure, including the April 2024 Muleshoe (Texas) water-tower incident.

overview: APT10 is a Chinese state-sponsored cyber-espionage group active since at least 2006. On 17 December 2018, the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment in the Southern District of New York charging Zhu Hua (aliases: Afwar, CVNX, Alayos, Godkiller) and Zhang Shilong (aliases: Baobeilong, Zhang Jianguo, Atreexp) with conspiracy to commit computer intrusion, wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. The indictment stated that both operatives worked for Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company in Tianjin and acted in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's (MSS) Tianjin State Security Bureau, aligning APT10 to MSS regional tasking rather than to a PLA unit.

The group is one of the most heavily aliased Chinese clusters. MITRE ATT&CK's canonical group card G0045 lists menuPass, Cicada, POTASSIUM, Stone Panda, Red Apollo, CVNX, HOGFISH and BRONZE RIVERSIDE. Symantec (Broadcom) tracks the actor as Cicada; CrowdStrike as Stone Panda; Microsoft historically as POTASSIUM. Since 2022, vendors have distinguished sub-clusters and umbrellas around it, including MirrorFace/Earth Kasha (ESET, Trend Micro) and Cuckoo Spear (Cybereason), treated as related to, or subgroups under, the APT10 umbrella.

APT10's signature contribution to the threat landscape is Operation Cloud Hopper, disclosed in April 2017 by PwC UK and BAE Systems, in which the actor systematically compromised Managed Service Providers (MSPs) to pivot into the customer networks they administered. The campaign gave APT10 broad, trusted access to intellectual property held by MSP clients across aerospace, manufacturing, healthcare, biotechnology, finance, telecoms and government, and it is credited by the US, UK, Japanese, Australian and Canadian governments as a decade-long IP-theft effort.

From 2019 onwards, APT10 activity has centred on Japan, delivered through the LODEINFO fileless backdoor (JPCERT/CC named the family in February 2020), the multi-layer Ecipekac/DESLoader/SigLoader chain feeding P8RAT and SodaMaster (Kaspersky A41APT, 2021), and, since 2023, the NOOPDOOR/NOOPLDR backdoor exposed by JPCERT/CC and Cybereason. Recent Trend Micro, ESET and JPCERT reporting attributes intrusions targeting Japanese manufacturers, defence contractors, media, political organisations and academia to sub-clusters (MirrorFace/Earth Kasha) that reuse APT10 code lineage and infrastructure.

attribution.text: The US Department of Justice, FBI, and multiple allied governments attribute APT10 to individuals acting in association with the Chinese Ministry of State Security's Tianjin State Security Bureau, working through Huaying Haitai Science and Technology Development Company in Tianjin. Zhu Hua and Zhang Shilong were charged by name in December 2018. Attribution is corroborated by MITRE ATT&CK, Symantec (Broadcom), FireEye/Mandiant and Kaspersky.

origin.text: The DoJ indictment states that from at least 2006 through 2018 the defendants conducted extensive intrusion campaigns for the MSS. MITRE lists first activity in 2006. PwC UK and BAE Systems assessed Cloud Hopper as in operation since at least 2014, with earlier menuPass activity dating to 2009.

mandate.text: Strategic intellectual-property theft and long-running political-military intelligence collection on behalf of the MSS. Targeting priorities have consistently favoured Japan and organisations linked to Japan, plus global supply-chain access through MSPs and, more recently, defence and academic research institutions in Japan, Taiwan and India.

name: Conti
description: Dissolved ransomware operation. Known for massive hospital attacks.

overview: Conti was a Russia-nexus, human-operated ransomware operation that emerged from the WIZARD SPIDER / TrickBot cybercrime ecosystem in mid-2020 as the successor to the Ryuk encryptor, and became the highest-earning and most prolific ransomware brand in the world before it publicly disintegrated in May 2022. MITRE ATT&CK catalogues the umbrella cluster under WIZARD SPIDER (G0102) — the CrowdStrike cryptonym for the same TrickBot / BazarBackdoor / Ryuk / Conti crew that Mandiant tracks as UNC1878, Microsoft as DEV-0193, and Secureworks as GOLD ULRICK; Conti is the ransomware family and the RaaS brand run inside that group.

Conti operated as a hybrid ransomware-as-a-service: a Russian-speaking core team in St Petersburg developed the encryptor, ran negotiations, and paid a fixed salary to full-time hackers who ran intrusions, while a smaller pool of affiliates rented access on a revenue-share basis. Initial access came from BazarLoader and TrickBot phishing implants, from IcedID, and from purchased access brokers; hands-on-keyboard operators then abused Cobalt Strike, PowerShell, PsExec and legitimate remote-management tools to move laterally, dump credentials with Mimikatz, exfiltrate to Mega or Rclone-fronted cloud storage, and finally deploy the Conti binary on both Windows hosts and VMware ESXi. Chainalysis and the US Treasury put Conti's known extortion revenue at more than USD 150 million between 2020 and 2022.

Two intrusions defined Conti's public reputation. In May 2021 the group crippled Ireland's Health Service Executive, forcing a nationwide shutdown of the HSE network and generating remediation costs the Irish government later put at over EUR 100 million; the FBI, CISA and the Irish PwC-led post-incident review all documented the attack. A year later, in April-May 2022, Conti attacked the government of Costa Rica in two waves, prompting President Rodrigo Chaves to declare a national state of emergency — the first ever declared by a state in response to a ransomware incident.

The operation collapsed on itself in early 2022. On 25 February 2022, one day after Russia invaded Ukraine, the Conti leadership blog posted a statement of 'full support' for the Russian government. A Ukrainian security researcher with existing access — the persona known as 'ContiLeaks' — retaliated by dumping more than a year of internal Jabber logs, source code, training documents and Bitcoin wallets to Twitter and public repositories. Between the ContiLeaks fallout, a USD 10 million Rewards for Justice bounty announced by the US State Department in May 2022, and coordinated US and UK sanctions against Trickbot / Conti members in February and September 2023, the Conti brand was formally retired by mid-2022 — but its personnel simply reorganised. Trellix, Mandiant and Group-IB trace Black Basta, BlackByte, KaraKurt, Zeon / Royal, HELLO KITTY and Silent Ransom (Luna Moth) directly to Conti alumni.

attribution.text: Attributed to a Russia-based criminal syndicate operating under the WIZARD SPIDER umbrella of the TrickBot / BazarBackdoor ecosystem. The US Treasury (OFAC), the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, MITRE ATT&CK, CrowdStrike, Mandiant and Microsoft all place the core operators inside Russia; the ContiLeaks chat logs geolocated the leadership team to St Petersburg. In February 2023 the US and UK jointly sanctioned seven named Russian nationals for their role in Trickbot / Conti operations, followed by an additional 11 designations in September 2023.

origin.text: First public sightings of the Conti ransomware family date to late May and early June 2020, when Carbon Black and VMware identified it as a successor to Ryuk sharing code, infrastructure and TrickBot delivery patterns. Wizard Spider itself, the parent crew, has been tracked by CrowdStrike since 2016 in connection with TrickBot; the Ryuk-to-Conti pivot completed during the second half of 2020.

mandate.text: Financially motivated: run a ransomware-as-a-service operation with double-extortion (encrypt + leak-site) monetisation, prioritise high-impact enterprise victims where downtime forces payment (hospitals, government, manufacturing, retail), and reinvest revenue into TrickBot/BazarBackdoor development and access-broker relationships. From 25 February 2022 onward the Conti leadership publicly aligned itself with the Russian state's position on the invasion of Ukraine, though independent analysts (Chainalysis, Mandiant, Group-IB) treat Conti as a criminal actor rather than a state proxy.

name: APT33
description: Iranian group focused on massive password spraying and cloud infrastructure abuse.

overview: APT33 is an Iranian state-sponsored cyber-espionage group publicly attributed to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), with tasking overlap in vendor reporting to the Nasr Institute contractor. Public reporting places its first observed activity around 2013; FireEye consolidated the cluster and published the initial attribution in September 2017 after identifying an operator handle (xman_1365_x) linked to Iranian hacking forums and a Nasr Institute employee.

The group is heavily aliased across the industry. MITRE ATT&CK catalogues it as APT33 (G0064) with the aliases Elfin (Symantec), Refined Kitten (CrowdStrike), Magnallium (Dragos) and HOLMIUM (the retired Microsoft cryptonym). In April 2023 Microsoft's revised naming taxonomy renamed HOLMIUM to Peach Sandstorm, and the majority of 2023-2024 reporting on the cluster now sits under that label. Proofpoint has also tracked overlapping activity as TA451.

APT33's mandate is strategic intelligence collection for the IRGC against Saudi Arabian, US, Israeli and Emirati aviation, aerospace, energy, defence, satellite communications and petrochemical targets, with a documented sideline in preparation of destructive tooling. Public reporting from FireEye, Kaspersky and Symantec has linked APT33 infrastructure and tools to the 2016-2017 Shamoon 2 wiper campaigns against Saudi Aramco and Sadara, and Trend Micro documented a shift in 2019 to reconnaissance of European industrial-control-system vendors, though vendors caveat the Shamoon overlap as infrastructure-and-personnel rather than a full identity match.

Since 2022 the cluster's operational tempo has been dominated by large-scale password-spraying under the Peach Sandstorm banner: a Microsoft advisory in September 2023 documented February-July 2023 password spray against thousands of tenants in the defence, satellite and pharmaceutical verticals, followed by exploitation of CVE-2022-47966 (Zoho ManageEngine) and CVE-2022-26134 (Atlassian Confluence) for on-premises access. In August 2024 Microsoft disclosed the custom Tickler multi-stage .NET backdoor deployed against satellite, communications equipment, oil-and-gas and government targets in the United States and the United Arab Emirates between April and July 2024, hosted on Azure infrastructure that the operators had signed up for using fraudulent Microsoft accounts, and paired with LinkedIn 'Smart Matches' recruitment lures.

attribution.text: Attributed to Iran and specifically to the IRGC, with FireEye's original 2017 report tying an operator handle used in the intrusions to a Nasr Institute employee working for the IRGC. Attribution has since been reinforced by Microsoft (HOLMIUM / Peach Sandstorm), CrowdStrike (Refined Kitten), Symantec (Elfin), Dragos (Magnallium), Kaspersky and MITRE ATT&CK. The US Treasury OFAC did not name APT33 by cryptonym in its Iran-related sanctions, but the CISA / US CyberCommand posture around Iranian state-linked cyber activity treats the cluster as an IRGC-aligned actor.

notableOperations.name: Tickler backdoor deployment (Apr-Jul 2024)
notableOperations.summary: Between April and July 2024 Peach Sandstorm deployed a new custom multi-stage .NET backdoor Microsoft named Tickler against satellite, communications equipment, oil-and-gas and federal / state-government targets in the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Two Tickler samples were analysed publicly. C2 ran on Azure App Service and Azure Storage tenants signed up by the attackers under fraudulent Microsoft accounts (Microsoft has since terminated the identified subscriptions), and the intrusions were fed by LinkedIn 'Smart Matches' recruiter-themed social engineering.

name: APT34
attribution: Iran â Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS); some vendor reporting notes overlap with IRGC-adjacent tasking
description: Iranian state-sponsored espionage cluster active since at least 2014 and one of the most consistently productive Middle Eastâfocused APTs. Attributed by MITRE, Mandiant and Microsoft to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Trademark tradecraft is DNS-tunnelling backdoors (Helminth, BONDUPDATER, ALMA Communicator, DNSpionage, Karkoff, Saitama) and abuse of on-premises Microsoft Exchange for credential theft and C2 (PowerExchange, StealHook). Persistent targeting of Iraqi, Saudi, UAE, Jordanian and Israeli government, telecom and energy sectors.

overview: APT34 â publicly named OilRig by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 in May 2016 and tracked by MITRE as G0049 â is an Iranian state-sponsored cyber-espionage cluster active since at least 2014. MITRE's canonical alias list is one of the longest in the framework: OilRig, COBALT GYPSY, APT34, Helix Kitten, Evasive Serpens, Hazel Sandstorm, EUROPIUM, ITG13, Earth Simnavaz, Crambus, TA452 and IRN2. In practice these names cover a decade of iterative campaigns against Iraqi, Saudi, UAE, Jordanian, Israeli, Lebanese and Turkish government, telecom, energy and financial targets, plus long-tail supply-chain intrusions used to pivot into those primary victims.

Attribution is centred on Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Mandiant, Microsoft and Palo Alto Unit 42 have separately assessed the group as MOIS-tasked based on target selection, operator time-zone analysis and the 2019 'Lab Dookhtegan' leak of internal OilRig tooling and victim data, which linked several operators to Iranian government-linked infrastructure. Some overlap with IRGC-adjacent activity has been noted around Iraq-focused campaigns, but the dominant public attribution remains MOIS. Under Microsoft's 2023 naming scheme the same cluster is Hazel Sandstorm; Symantec calls it Crambus; Trend Micro tracks a subset as Earth Simnavaz.

OilRig's signature tradecraft is DNS-tunnelling backdoors and heavy reliance on legitimate-looking Excel/Word spearphish with malicious macros. The Unit 42 catalogue is unusually deep: Helminth (2016), ISMDoor and BONDUPDATER/POWRUNER (2017), OopsIE, RGDoor and QUADAGENT (2018), ALMA Communicator (2017-2018), DNSpionage and Karkoff (2018-2019 in Cisco Talos reporting). Later campaigns kept DNS as an evasion channel â Fortinet's Saitama (2022) used DNS finite-state-machine C2 against Jordan's foreign ministry â and layered in abuse of reputable cloud services (Microsoft Exchange, OneDrive, Office 365 accounts) for downloader and C2 traffic that blends into normal enterprise flows (ESET's OilBooster/OilCheck/ODAgent, Trend Micro's Menorah).

Since the 2019 Lab Dookhtegan leak the group has rebuilt and expanded, not retreated. Symantec's October 2023 Crambus write-up documented an eight-month intrusion in a Middle Eastern government where PowerExchange watched an Exchange mailbox and executed operator commands sent as email; Check Point's September 2024 report catalogued Veaty and Spearal, two custom families used against Iraqi ministry networks; Trend Micro's October 2024 Earth Simnavaz report showed the group chaining Windows kernel CVE-2024-30088 with password-filter DLLs and the StealHook Exchange backdoor to exfiltrate credentials from Gulf-state government tenants. The trajectory is a decade of steady iteration on the same DNS-plus-Exchange playbook rather than any pivot away from it.

The 2019 'Lab Dookhtegan' Telegram leak of OilRig source code, victim lists and operator handles reinforced the MOIS assessment. name: APT38
description: Specialized in massive bank heists via SWIFT. $1.1B+ attempted, $100M+ stolen.

overview: APT38 is the North Korean state-sponsored cluster specialised in financially motivated intrusions against banks, ATM networks and cryptocurrency exchanges. MITRE ATT&CK catalogues it as APT38 (G0082); Kaspersky and Malpedia track the same actor under the older cryptonym Bluenoroff; CrowdStrike calls it Stardust Chollima; Proofpoint tracks a partially overlapping cluster as TA444; Microsoft calls it Sapphire Sleet (previously COPERNICIUM); and Mandiant maps APT38 under the broader Lazarus umbrella as one of several distinct DPRK sub-teams. The group is subordinate to the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) Ã¢ the DPRK's principal foreign-intelligence service Ã¢ and public reporting places its tasking in the RGB's 3rd Bureau / Lab 110 financial-crime cell.

Public reporting places APT38's earliest documented activity around 2014, with the cluster becoming globally visible after the February 2016 Bangladesh Bank SWIFT heist, in which operators used forged SWIFT messages to attempt to transfer USD 951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the New York Federal Reserve Ã¢ of which USD 81 million was successfully moved through the Philippines and largely laundered through casinos. BAE Systems and Symantec independently attributed the intrusion to a DPRK cluster in April-May 2016, Kaspersky consolidated the tooling under Bluenoroff in April 2017, and Mandiant formally coined the APT38 name in its October 2018 report 'APT38: Un-usual Suspects'.

APT38's mandate is revenue generation for the DPRK regime under UN and US sanctions: SWIFT-message manipulation against tier-2 and tier-3 correspondent banks, coordinated ATM cash-out schemes tracked by CISA as FASTCash / BeagleBoyz, fraudulent cryptocurrency trading apps (Operation AppleJeus), decentralised-finance bridge and exchange thefts, and targeted social engineering of cryptocurrency and defence-industry employees. The US Department of Justice unsealed a criminal complaint against Park Jin Hyok (September 2018) and a superseding indictment naming Jon Chang Hyok, Kim Il and Park Jin Hyok (February 2021) that formally charges the RGB's Unit 110 with the Bangladesh Bank, Sony Pictures and WannaCry operations and multiple cryptocurrency thefts. The US Treasury has repeatedly sanctioned the cluster, its front companies (Chinyong / Yanbian Silverstar) and its money-laundering pipeline through OFAC actions from 2019 to 2025.

Since 2022 the group has kept up an extraordinary operational tempo against the crypto sector: the USD 620-625 million Ronin Bridge (Axie Infinity) hack of March 2022, the USD 100 million Harmony Horizon Bridge theft of June 2022, the USD 235 million WazirX intrusion (July 2024), and the record USD 1.46-1.5 billion Bybit theft (February 2025), each of which the FBI publicly attributed to the DPRK / TraderTraitor / APT38 sub-cluster. Vendor reporting from Chainalysis, Mandiant, Kaspersky, NCC Group, Proofpoint, Trend Micro and JPCERT/CC has tied these operations to a consistent tradecraft: LinkedIn/Telegram recruitment lures, malicious npm and PyPI packages under the Contagious Interview and DangerousPassword campaigns, trojanised Electron and Node desktop apps for macOS and Windows, and AppleJeus-family cryptocurrency trading apps.

attribution.text: Attributed to the DPRK Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB), specifically to Lab 110 / Unit 110 (also referred to as the 3rd Bureau / 121st Bureau financial-crime cell). Attribution has been made by the US Department of Justice through the September 2018 Park Jin Hyok criminal complaint and the February 2021 Jon Chang Hyok / Kim Il / Park Jin Hyok superseding indictment, by the US Department of the Treasury through repeated OFAC designations (September 2019, April 2022, May 2023, November 2023, November 2024), by CISA/FBI/USCYBERCOM in the AA20-239A BeagleBoyz advisory and the AA22-108A TraderTraitor advisory, and reinforced by Mandiant, Kaspersky, CrowdStrike, Microsoft, Proofpoint, Trend Micro, Chainalysis and MITRE ATT&CK.

notableOperations.name: Bangladesh Bank SWIFT heist
notableOperations.summary: On 4-5 February 2016 operators used stolen SWIFT credentials and a bespoke implant that patched the Alliance Access transaction-log printer to submit 35 fraudulent MT103 payment orders totalling USD 951 million from Bangladesh Bank's account at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. USD 81 million cleared to accounts at RCBC in Manila before Deutsche Bank flagged a typo in one transfer, and the funds were laundered through Philippine casinos. BAE Systems, Symantec, Kaspersky and Mandiant attributed the operation to APT38 / Bluenoroff; the 2018 Park Jin Hyok complaint and 2021 superseding indictment charged individual RGB operators.

notableOperations.name: Far Eastern International Bank (FEIB) SWIFT heist
notableOperations.summary: In October 2017 operators compromised Taiwan's Far Eastern International Bank and issued fraudulent SWIFT payment orders for USD 60 million to accounts in Sri Lanka, Cambodia and the United States. Almost all of the funds were frozen and recovered; the Sri Lankan money-mule was arrested. Symantec and BAE Systems linked the intrusion to APT38 through malware overlap with the Bangladesh Bank operation and re-use of the SWIFT Alliance Access transaction-log manipulation technique.

notableOperations.name: FASTCash / BeagleBoyz ATM cash-out
notableOperations.summary: Multi-year cluster of coordinated ATM cash-out schemes against retail-payment switching applications running on IBM AIX and Windows (FASTCash and FASTCash 2.0). Operators compromised bank card-authorisation systems, planted an implant that intercepted ISO 8583 messages, and issued 'approved' responses to hundreds of coordinated mule withdrawals. A single 2018 operation cashed out an estimated USD 13.5 million from Cosmos Bank India across 28 countries in two hours. CISA, FBI, USCYBERCOM and Treasury tracked the operators as BeagleBoyz in the August 2020 AA20-239A advisory and estimated attempted takes above USD 2 billion since 2015.

notableOperations.name: Operation AppleJeus Ã¢ fraudulent cryptocurrency trading apps
notableOperations.summary: Long-running campaign in which APT38 / Bluenoroff / TraderTraitor operators built and distributed fake cryptocurrency trading applications for Windows and macOS (Celas Trade Pro, JMT Trading, Union Crypto Trader, Kupay Wallet, CoinGoTrade, Dorusio, Ants2Whale, TokenAIS, CryptAIS, RaiseFX and successors). Each shipped a signed Electron / Node wrapper around a legitimate-looking trading UI, chained to a second-stage macOS/Windows backdoor for reconnaissance and wallet theft against cryptocurrency exchanges, funds and individual traders. Kaspersky's AppleJeus reports and the CISA/FBI/Treasury AA21-048A advisory documented over a dozen successor variants.

notableOperations.name: Ronin Bridge (Axie Infinity) heist
notableOperations.summary: On 23 March 2022 operators using a fake LinkedIn recruiter approach against a Sky Mavis engineer obtained access to five of the nine Ronin validator private keys and drained 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC (approximately USD 620-625 million at time of theft) from the Ronin Bridge supporting the Axie Infinity game. The US Treasury attributed the theft to the DPRK / Lazarus / APT38 on 14 April 2022 (OFAC action JY0708), designating the Ethereum wallet used and adding Chainalysis-tracked laundering infrastructure. This is the single largest DeFi-bridge theft to date besides Bybit and Poly Network.

notableOperations.name: Harmony Horizon Bridge heist
notableOperations.summary: On 23-24 June 2022 operators drained approximately USD 100 million in ETH, BNB, USDC and other assets from the Harmony Horizon cross-chain bridge after compromising two of the bridge's five multisig private keys. The FBI publicly attributed the operation to the Lazarus / APT38 / TraderTraitor cluster on 23 January 2023 and traced Ren Protocol and Railgun laundering flows. notableOperations.name: DangerousPassword / Contagious Interview supply-chain and social-engineering cluster
notableOperations.summary: Sustained social-engineering campaign against cryptocurrency, DeFi and Web3 developers under overlapping brand names DangerousPassword (JPCERT/CC), Contagious Interview (Palo Alto Unit 42), CryptoCore (ClearSky) and Sapphire Sleet (Microsoft). Operators pose as recruiters or venture-fund associates on LinkedIn, Telegram, X and Signal; walk targets through fake technical interviews or 'debug my code' tasks that pull malicious npm, PyPI or GitHub-hosted Node modules (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie); and pivot from developer workstations to production wallet-signing infrastructure. NCC Group, Kaspersky, Proofpoint (TA444) and JPCERT/CC have documented dozens of trojanised packages and installers.

name: Kimsuky
description: Massive phishing campaigns against researchers and academics.

overview: Kimsuky is a North Korean state-sponsored cyber-espionage cluster attributed to the Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB), the DPRK's principal foreign intelligence service. Public reporting from CISA/FBI, Mandiant and the US Treasury dates first observed activity to 2012 and consistently ties the group to strategic intelligence collection on foreign policy, national-security and nuclear-policy topics tied to the Korean Peninsula. On 30 November 2023 the US Treasury (OFAC) formally sanctioned Kimsuky, explicitly describing it as subordinate to the UN- and US-designated RGB.

The cluster is heavily aliased: MITRE (G0094) tracks it as Kimsuky / Velvet Chollima / Black Banshee / THALLIUM, Microsoft calls it Emerald Sleet, Proofpoint tracks a large sub-cluster as TA427 (previously TA406/TA408), Mandiant elevated a partially overlapping cluster to APT43 in March 2023 as a self-funded espionage-plus-cryptocurrency-laundering operator, and CrowdStrike uses Springtail. Public reporting treats the boundary between these designations as fuzzy but overlapping; the RGB tasking and the AppleSeed / BabyShark / GoldDragon toolset are the common thread.

Kimsuky is generally regarded as the DPRK's most prolific spear-phishing operator. Its primary victim set is South Korean, Japanese and US think tanks, academics, journalists, defectors and North Korea policy researchers, but also government agencies (notably the South Korean Ministry of Unification), defense contractors, nuclear operators (KHNP, 2014) and, during 2020, pharmaceutical companies working on COVID-19 vaccines. The group is only medium in raw technical sophistication compared to Lazarus/APT38, but its operational tempo, tailored social engineering (often over long-running benign 'rapport-building' conversations) and abuse of loose DMARC policies make it exceptionally hard to defend against for the target population.

The 2023-2025 arc shows a clear evolution: AhnLab, S2W and Kaspersky have documented a shift from the historical HWP/VBS/HTA chains toward Go-based tooling (GoBear, Troll Stealer, Gomir), reconnaissance modules (ReconShark, May 2023), malicious Chrome extensions (TRANSLATEXT, disclosed by Zscaler in June 2024), RDP-wrapper and forceCopy credential-theft utilities (early 2025), and the ClickFix PowerShell social-engineering tactic (Q1 2025). Microsoft additionally reported in February 2024 that Emerald Sleet was using OpenAI-hosted LLMs to research vulnerabilities and draft phishing lures â one of the first publicly documented LLM-abuse cases by any nation-state actor.

attribution.text: Attributed to the DPRK's Reconnaissance General Bureau (RGB) by the US Department of the Treasury (OFAC designation, 30 November 2023), CISA/FBI/US Cyber Command (AA20-301A) and the June 2023 State Department / FBI / NSA / NIS / DSA / NPA joint advisory on DPRK social engineering. The 121st Bureau assignment is widely reported by researchers but not confirmed by any government advisory.

name: DarkHotel
description: Selective targeting of executives via luxury hotel Wi-Fi in Asia-Pacific.

overview: DarkHotel is a long-running cyber-espionage cluster that Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) first exposed publicly in November 2014 under the eponymous 'Darkhotel APT' report. The group is tracked by MITRE ATT&CK as G0012 with the aliases DUBNIUM (Microsoft), Karba, Tapaoux and Luder (Kaspersky, Symantec, ESET) and Nemim (Trend Micro). The Chinese threat-intelligence community catalogues the same or an overlapping cluster as APT-C-06.

The signature technique that gave the group its name is the compromise of luxury hotel Wi-Fi networks in Asia-Pacific to intercept and spearphish specific corporate executives on business travel. Kaspersky documented forged Adobe/Google/Microsoft update prompts injected into hotel captive portals, backed by stolen or forged digital certificates from Deutsche Telekom, Digisign, TechnoTrust and Cyberoam. Alongside the hotel operations, DarkHotel has run parallel spearphishing waves with malicious HTA/office attachments (Inexsmar), several browser zero-days, and post-2018 targeting of Chinese government agencies, VPN providers and Ã¢ during the pandemic Ã¢ the World Health Organization.

Attribution is not settled at the government level. Kaspersky's original 2014 report and its 2015 update noted Korean-language artefacts and code-page markers pointing toward Korean-speaking operators; multiple vendors and Wikipedia have subsequently characterised the cluster as 'suspected South Korean'. No government has publicly endorsed that attribution, and Chinese vendors (QiAnXin, Antiy) prefer the neutral APT-C-06 designation. The apt.etda.or.th community card summarises the state of play as 'unknown; suspected South Korea' and this ficha follows that framing.

The group's operational tempo has stayed high across 15+ years of documented activity, including 2019-2020 exploitation of Internet Explorer zero-days CVE-2019-1367 and CVE-2020-0674, and 2020 reporting by Reuters of intrusion attempts against WHO officials during the COVID-19 response.

name: Turla
description: Active since 2004. Expert in watering holes and hijacking other APTs infrastructure.

overview: Turla is a Russian state-sponsored cyber-espionage group, one of the oldest and most technically sophisticated actors in the public record. Public reporting and multiple governments (US, UK, Estonia, Czech Republic) attribute Turla to Center 16 of the Russian FSB (Federal Security Service), the successor to the KGB signals-intelligence directorate. Microsoft tracks the cluster as Secret Blizzard; other vendor aliases include Snake, Uroburos, Waterbug (Symantec), Venomous Bear (CrowdStrike), Krypton and WhiteBear.

Turla is generally treated as the descendant of the 1996-1999 Moonlight Maze intrusions against US defence and research networks â the first named state-sponsored cyber-espionage campaign in history. In 2017 Kaspersky/King's College London published forensic evidence linking Turla's Linux Penquin backdoor to LOKI2 tooling used in Moonlight Maze, giving the group a documented lineage of more than 25 years of continuous operation.

The group is known for platform-level engineering rather than opportunistic tradecraft: the Snake / Uroburos rootkit is a modular kernel-mode implant with peer-to-peer C2 that ran for a decade before the FBI dismantled its global network in Operation Medusa (May 2023). Turla has also pioneered highly unusual command-and-control channels, most famously the hijacking of legitimate satellite internet downlinks (2015), and has repeatedly parasitised the infrastructure of other threat actors â most publicly the December 2024 Microsoft/Mandiant disclosure that Secret Blizzard was piggybacking on Pakistan-nexus Storm-0156 servers to reach South-Asian government targets.

Turla's mission set is classical strategic espionage: foreign ministries and embassies (LightNeuron Exchange backdoor, Crutch/Dropbox exfiltration), defence ministries, research and academia, and â since 2022 â Ukrainian military systems in the wake of Russia's invasion. Its malware families (Snake, ComRAT/Agent.BTZ, Carbon, Kazuar, Gazer, HyperStack, Crutch, TinyTurla, TinyTurla-NG, LunarWeb/LunarMail) form one of the most-studied APT toolchains in the industry.

attribution.text: Attributed to Center 16 of the Russian FSB by the US FBI, NSA, CISA and DoJ in the May 2023 Snake takedown, and independently corroborated by Microsoft, Mandiant, ESET, Kaspersky, CrowdStrike and Symantec across a decade of technical reporting.

name: APT32
description: Vietnamese espionage against regional adversaries and human rights activists.

overview: APT32 is a Vietnamese state-tasked cyber-espionage cluster active since at least 2012 whose collection priorities align with the Vietnamese government's political and industrial interests. Mandiant/FireEye publicly consolidated the group under the APT32 designation in May 2017, and MITRE ATT&CK catalogues it as G0050. Public reporting also tracks the same activity under OceanLotus and SeaLotus (Kaspersky, ESET, Volexity), APT-C-00 (Qihoo 360), Ocean Buffalo (CrowdStrike), Cobalt Kitty (Cybereason) and BISMUTH â since Microsoft's April 2023 rename, Canvas Cyclone (Microsoft Threat Intelligence).

The group's targeting bundles three lines of effort. First, foreign multinationals with material interests in Vietnam â automotive, hospitality, consumer products and manufacturing â with Toyota, Hyundai and several German carmakers named in public reporting between 2019 and 2020. Second, regional political targets: ASEAN neighbours, Cambodia's political opposition around the 2017-2018 elections, the Philippines, and Chinese government entities during the early phase of the COVID-19 outbreak. Third, sustained surveillance operations against Vietnamese dissidents, human-rights defenders, bloggers and diaspora journalists, documented in detail by Amnesty International, the EFF and Citizen Lab.

APT32 tradecraft is notable for its OPSEC discipline and platform breadth. Operators run parallel Windows and macOS toolchains (Denis / KerrDown / Cobalt Strike loaders on Windows; OceanLotus / OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D on macOS), rely on signed-binary DLL side-loading through McAfee, Symantec and Microsoft-branded executables, and heavily obfuscate PowerShell stagers. Command-and-control frequently rides legitimate cloud services (Dropbox, Google Drive, GitHub) and short-lived typosquatted domains, and the group has repeatedly deployed strategic web compromises on real ASEAN media, NGO and government sites (the 2017-2020 'OceanLotus Blossoms' and fake-news-portal campaigns documented by Volexity).

Since 2020 APT32's public profile has centred on three episodes. In April 2020 FireEye reported that the group had targeted China's Ministry of Emergency Management and the Wuhan provincial government during the first weeks of the COVID-19 outbreak, in what BlackBerry and Volexity separately characterised as pandemic-intelligence collection. Later that year Microsoft's November 2020 BISMUTH advisory described the group deploying Monero coin miners inside government and academic victims in France and Vietnam as noisy cover for espionage tasking. And through 2021-2024, EFF, Amnesty and Access Now documented continuing spyware and phishing operations against Vietnamese activists at home and abroad, with the group's tooling still recognisably descended from the 2017 Mandiant baseline.

attribution.text: Attributed to the Vietnamese government by Mandiant/FireEye (May 2017), reinforced by Volexity, CrowdStrike (Ocean Buffalo), Microsoft (BISMUTH / Canvas Cyclone), Kaspersky, ESET, Amnesty International and the EFF. No public indictment has yet been unsealed and no specific Vietnamese ministry or unit has been named at government level in an attribution statement; the specific tasking body is generally described as 'the Vietnamese state' or 'a Vietnamese-government-aligned actor'.

name: Hafnium
description: 4 Microsoft Exchange zero-days. 30,000+ organizations compromised in days.

overview: Hafnium is the Microsoft-assigned cryptonym for the People's Republic of China state-sponsored cluster that mass-exploited four Microsoft Exchange Server zero-days (ProxyLogon: CVE-2021-26855, CVE-2021-26857, CVE-2021-26858 and CVE-2021-27065) in early 2021. Volexity discovered active exploitation on 6 January 2021 and reported it privately to Microsoft; DEVCORE independently reported the SSRF pre-auth chain on 5 January 2021; Microsoft released out-of-band patches on 2 March 2021, at which point the operators shifted from a targeted campaign into an indiscriminate global sweep. By the time CISA issued Emergency Directive 21-02 on 3 March 2021, tens of thousands of on-premises Exchange servers had been backdoored with China Chopper and ASPXSpy web shells.

MITRE catalogues the group as HAFNIUM (G0125). Microsoft's July 2023 threat-actor naming taxonomy renamed the cluster Silk Typhoon under the 'Typhoon' family for China-nexus actors, and the two names now refer to the same tracking (Hafnium retained as historical). Public reporting also references the ProxyLogon operation as 'Operation Exchange Marauder' (Volexity) and, historically, aliases the ETDA / Thai CERT card lists alongside Zirconium overlap claims that MITRE has never adopted.

On 19 July 2021 the United States, the United Kingdom, the European Union, NATO, Australia, Canada, Japan and New Zealand issued a coordinated attribution naming the PRC Ministry of State Security (MSS) as responsible for the Exchange campaign. The same day the US Department of Justice unsealed an indictment of four MSS Hainan State Security Department (HSSD) officers for a separate multi-year intrusion campaign (APT40), and CISA / FBI / NSA published joint advisory AA21-200A cataloguing MSS-affiliated tradecraft targeting US and allied networks. Hafnium itself has not (as of September 2026) been the subject of a public indictment naming individual operators, but Treasury / OFAC sanctioned Shanghai-based cyber actor Yin Kecheng on 17 January 2025 for direct involvement in the Department of the Treasury network compromise later attributed by Microsoft to Silk Typhoon.

From late 2023 the cluster shifted materially away from mass Exchange exploitation and toward a supply-chain / IT-services intrusion model. In December 2024 the operators used stolen credentials and API keys taken from BeyondTrust's Remote Support SaaS platform (CVE-2024-12356 command-injection, added to CISA KEV on 19 December 2024) to reach into the Department of the Treasury's departmental office and OFAC. Microsoft's 5 March 2025 report 'Silk Typhoon targeting IT supply chain' formalised the pivot: n-day and zero-day exploitation of Ivanti Pulse Connect Secure (CVE-2025-0282), Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect (CVE-2024-3400), Citrix NetScaler ADC (CVE-2023-3519), and routine abuse of stolen cloud application secrets to pivot laterally from IT vendors into their downstream customers.

Hafnium / Silk Typhoon's mandate is strategic espionage against sectors that produce intelligence of interest to the MSS: infectious-disease research (with pronounced activity against COVID-19 vaccine researchers during the original 2020-2021 wave), higher education, law firms, defence industrial base, policy think tanks, non-governmental organisations, and â since 2024 â the IT / managed-service / identity-provider supply chain that fans out into US and allied government customers.

attribution.text: Attributed to the People's Republic of China Ministry of State Security. The US, UK, EU, NATO, Australia, Canada, Japan and New Zealand made a coordinated public attribution on 19 July 2021 naming the MSS as responsible for the Microsoft Exchange (ProxyLogon) exploitation campaign. On 17 January 2025 US Treasury / OFAC sanctioned Shanghai-based Yin Kecheng for his direct involvement in the Department of the Treasury compromise later attributed by Microsoft to Silk Typhoon. Reinforced by Microsoft MSTIC, Volexity, Mandiant, ESET, ETDA / Thai CERT and MITRE ATT&CK.

Volexity's independent discovery of the SSRF-driven Exchange exploitation on 6 January 2021, and DEVCORE's parallel bug-report submission to Microsoft on 5 January 2021, are the earliest publicly documented Hafnium activity. Public reporting places the group's operational history at 'at least 2020' â with pre-ProxyLogon reconnaissance against COVID-19 research organisations attributed by Microsoft to the same actor.

notableOperations.name: Operation Exchange Marauder (ProxyLogon)
notableOperations.summary: Discovery on 6 January 2021 by Volexity of active pre-auth exploitation of Microsoft Exchange Server via CVE-2021-26855 (SSRF), CVE-2021-26857 (Unified Messaging deserialisation), CVE-2021-26858 and CVE-2021-27065 (post-auth arbitrary file write). Microsoft shipped out-of-band patches on 2 March 2021; within 24-48 hours the operators shifted from a targeted campaign into an indiscriminate global sweep and Krebs on Security reported that at least 30,000 US organisations had been backdoored, with worldwide estimates running to 250,000+ Exchange servers.

notableOperations.name: US Treasury / OFAC compromise via BeyondTrust (Silk Typhoon)

name: Volt Typhoon
description: Pre-positioning in US critical infrastructure for future sabotage. Living-off-the-land.

overview: Volt Typhoon is a People's Republic of China state-sponsored cyber activity cluster that Microsoft, CISA, the FBI and NSA jointly attribute to strategic pre-positioning inside United States critical infrastructure. Microsoft's May 2023 disclosure placed the group's first observed activity in mid-2021 and reported that it had, by that point, obtained access to communications, manufacturing, utility, transportation, construction, maritime, government, information technology and education sector networks in the continental US and Guam. Unlike most Chinese espionage groups, whose collection is intelligence-led, Volt Typhoon's tradecraft, target selection and persistence choices are consistent with pre-positioning for disruptive or destructive effects during a future crisis, most notably in the Indo-Pacific.

The cluster is tracked under several vendor cryptonyms that describe overlapping tradecraft rather than fully congruent identities: Vanguard Panda (CrowdStrike), BRONZE SILHOUETTE (Secureworks), Insidious Taurus (Palo Alto Unit 42), DEV-0391 later Volt Typhoon (Microsoft) and VOLTZITE for the ICS/OT slice (Dragos). MITRE catalogues the group as G1017 and Malpedia as volt_typhoon. Because these vendor clusters were merged over time as evidence accumulated, older reporting under Vanguard Panda or BRONZE SILHOUETTE (2021-2023) should be read as the same activity Microsoft and CISA later named Volt Typhoon.

Volt Typhoon's signature is Living-off-the-Land (LOTL) tradecraft executed with unusual discipline. Rather than deploying custom implants, operators chain built-in Windows binaries (wmic, ntdsutil, netsh, netstat, tracert, ping, whoami, nltest, PowerShell) and off-the-shelf open-source tooling to blend into normal administrator activity. Initial access is repeatedly documented against internet-exposed edge devices, including Fortinet FortiGuard-40F, Ivanti Connect Secure, Citrix and Cisco appliances, and Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus (CVE-2021-40539). Once inside they extract credentials from LSASS and the NTDS.dit domain database, move laterally over impacketised WMI/PsExec, stage data in innocuous-looking archive files and exfiltrate over compromised third-party infrastructure. CISA's February 2024 joint advisory documented dwell times of at least five years inside some victims.

Command-and-control traffic is proxied through the KV Botnet, a covert relay network built out of end-of-life SOHO routers (Cisco RV, DrayTek Vigor, NETGEAR ProSAFE) that Lumen Black Lotus Labs first exposed in December 2023. The FBI and Justice Department disrupted a large tranche of that infrastructure on 31 January 2024 under Operation Dying Ember, and Director Wray used a same-day appearance before the House Select Committee on the CCP to warn that PRC hacking of US critical infrastructure was at 'a scale greater than we'd seen before'. CISA and partners followed with the AA24-038A 'urgent action' advisory a week later, and Dragos has continued to track VOLTZITE activity against US electric and water utilities into 2024-2026.

attribution.text: Attributed to People's Republic of China state-sponsored actors by Microsoft (May 2023), the joint CISA/NSA/FBI advisory AA23-144A, and reinforced by the February 2024 joint advisory AA24-038A signed by CISA, NSA, FBI, DoE, EPA, TSA and Five Eyes partners. FBI Director Wray publicly attributed the activity to PRC state hackers in January 2024 Congressional testimony. Vendor telemetry places the operator inside the People's Liberation Army sphere; several assessments propose an association with the PLA's Strategic Support Force / Cyberspace Force, though this specific unit assignment is not publicly confirmed at government level.

mandate.text: Pre-positioning inside US and allied critical infrastructure for the purpose of enabling disruptive or destructive cyber effects during a future geopolitical crisis, in particular a Taiwan or wider Indo-Pacific contingency. CISA's February 2024 advisory states that Volt Typhoon actors 'are seeking to pre-position themselves on IT networks for disruptive or destructive cyberattacks against U.S. critical infrastructure in the event of a major crisis or conflict with the United States'. The operational mandate is disruption-enabling access rather than the intelligence-collection mandate typical of other Chinese state groups.

notableOperations.name: KV Botnet SOHO router relay network
notableOperations.summary: Lumen Black Lotus Labs disclosed on 13 December 2023 that a covert botnet built out of end-of-life Cisco RV320/RV325, DrayTek Vigor and NETGEAR ProSAFE SOHO routers was being used to proxy Volt Typhoon operations. The KV cluster served as an anonymising relay layer that made the operator's traffic appear to originate from residential IP space inside the target country. A companion 'JDY' cluster was used for reconnaissance.

notableOperations.name: Operation Dying Ember â FBI/DoJ KV Botnet takedown
notableOperations.summary: On 31 January 2024 the US Department of Justice and FBI announced a court-authorised operation that disrupted the KV Botnet by remotely removing the malware from hundreds of compromised US-based Cisco and NETGEAR SOHO routers, using the same admin interfaces the operator relied on. Attorney General Garland and Director Wray framed the operation as blunting Volt Typhoon's ability to hide inside US infrastructure. Lumen documented a partial rebuild attempt weeks later ('don't call it a comeback').

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
techniques.usage: Signature Living-off-the-Land approach: heavy reliance on signed built-in Windows binaries (wmic, ntdsutil, netsh, cmd, PowerShell) to avoid dropping bespoke malware onto disk.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
techniques.usage: Moves laterally within Active Directory environments by re-using stolen NTLM hashes rather than cracking passwords, again to avoid alerting on interactive logons.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
techniques.usage: Uses ntdsutil to create an install-from-media snapshot of the domain controller and exfiltrate NTDS.dit for offline hash cracking, providing enterprise-wide credential material.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys
techniques.usage: Extracts SSH keys and other private-key material from compromised hosts and stolen backups to enable authenticated pivoting through the environment.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.usage: Enumerates local and domain accounts with net user, net group, whoami and nltest /domain_trusts to map privilege paths inside Active Directory.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.usage: Scans internal networks with living-off-the-land tools and open-source utilities (Fast Reverse Proxy, Impacket) to map lateral targets and jump hosts.

techniques.name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
techniques.usage: Proxies command-and-control traffic through the KV Botnet SOHO-router relay layer so that traffic entering victim networks originates from residential IP space in the target country.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.usage: Delivers open-source tools (Impacket, Fast Reverse Proxy 'frp', Mimikatz) to compromised hosts using LOLBin fetches such as certutil and PowerShell IEX.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.usage: Compresses staged files with archivers such as WinRAR or 7-Zip prior to exfiltration to reduce volume and disguise sensitive content as routine archives.

techniques.name: Data Staged
techniques.usage: Stages collected files under masqueraded paths on domain controllers or file servers before archiving and exfiltrating, taking advantage of legitimate administrative shares.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.usage: Clears Security, System and PowerShell event logs with wevtutil cl and Clear-EventLog to erase evidence of ntdsutil and LSASS access.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
techniques.usage: Deletes staged archives, hash dumps and dropped tools after exfiltration to minimise forensic residue on compromised hosts.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.usage: Renames malicious binaries and staged output to look like Windows updates or system files, and drops tooling under paths that mimic legitimate Microsoft directories.

name: Mustang Panda
description: Chinese espionage focused on ASEAN, Mongolia and Southeast Asia. Targeting minorities and dissidents.

overview: Mustang Panda is a China-nexus cyber-espionage cluster active since at least 2012 (MITRE ATT&CK G0129) and one of the most heavily aliased actors in threat intelligence: Bronze President (Secureworks), TA416 (Proofpoint), RedDelta (Recorded Future / Insikt), Earth Preta (Trend Micro), Camaro Dragon (Check Point), Stately Taurus (Palo Alto Unit 42), HoneyMyte (Kaspersky / Sophos), Twill Typhoon (Microsoft), HIVE0154 (IBM X-Force) and â under Google TAG's 2024/2026 naming schemes â UNC6384 / TEMP.Hex. The US Department of Justice's January 2025 unsealed operation states plainly that the PRC government pays the operators to develop a Mustang Panda-specific version of PlugX, placing the group in the PLA / MSS contractor orbit rather than treating it as an independent actor.

Targeting is consistent across a decade of public reporting: government ministries, diplomatic missions, NGOs, think tanks and religious institutions in Southeast Asia (Myanmar, Vietnam, the Philippines, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan), Mongolia, Pakistan, the Vatican and Catholic organisations linked to Hong Kong, and â from February 2022 onwards, as Russia amassed troops on Ukraine's border â European foreign ministries, EU institutions and organisations delivering services to Ukrainian refugees. ESET, Cisco Talos, Proofpoint and Check Point all independently observed the pivot toward Europe as Beijing's collection requirements followed the war.

The group's signature tradecraft is legitimate-signed-executable DLL sideloading (T1574.001) paired with a rolling family of PlugX / Korplug derivatives â RedDelta PlugX, Hodur, THOR, DOPLUGS, TONESHELL, PUBLOAD, MQsTTang, FDMTP, HIUPAN, PTSOCKET and, in 2024-2026, SplatCloak / SplatDropper, StarProxy and the FDMTP 3.x modular framework. Delivery has cycled through Google Drive links, Dropbox, malicious .LNK-in-RAR bundles, HTML smuggling (SmugX), TP-Link SOHO router firmware implants (Camaro Dragon's Horse Shell), USB worms (HIUPAN, WispRider, MISTCLOAK) and â in the 2026 Darktrace campaign â CDN-look-alike C2 over the custom Duplex Message Transport Protocol (DMTP).

Disruption has failed to slow the cluster. In January 2025 the DoJ and FBI, working with French police and Sekoia.io, executed nine rolling warrants to command Mustang Panda's own PlugX variant to self-delete from roughly 4,258 US machines. Within months Trend Micro, Darktrace and Cisco Talos were tracking fresh Twill Typhoon / Earth Preta activity across APAC and Europe using rotated infrastructure and new loaders, confirming the assessment that the group's execution model â DLL sideloading plus modular PlugX plus removable-media propagation â persists across infrastructure and payload churn.

attribution.text: Attributed to a People's Republic of China state-sponsored group by the US Department of Justice (January 2025), the FBI, French national police (with Sekoia.io), MITRE ATT&CK and every major western vendor. The DoJ affidavit states that the PRC government paid the Mustang Panda operators to develop the specific PlugX variant used against US, European, Asian and Chinese-dissident targets since at least 2014. Microsoft tracks the cluster as Twill Typhoon within its 'China-based nation-state actor' taxonomy.
