techniques.usage: Chains Windows Quick Assist for hands-on-keyboard entry, then persists with AnyDesk, ScreenConnect, TeamViewer or Splashtop pushed via PowerShell installers.

sources.title: Ongoing Social Engineering Campaign Linked to Black Basta

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.usage: PowerShell one-liners invoked from Quick Assist sessions to fetch SystemBC and Cobalt Strike loaders; also used to disable Defender via Set-MpPreference.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.usage: Batch scripts (dark.bat, del.bat) chained through PsExec to push the encryptor across every reachable host during the ransomware stage.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.usage: The Black Basta encryptor installs itself as a Windows service (typically named after a legitimate process) and configures itself to run at safe-mode boot before encryption.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.usage: Deploys the FIN7-authored AvNeutralizer / AuKill EDR-killer, abusing the Process Explorer driver (procexp.sys) and later Windows' TTD Monitor (ProcLaunchMon.sys) to terminate protected security processes.

sources.title: Black Basta EDR Evasion Tied to FIN7

techniques.name: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification
techniques.usage: Reboots the host into Safe Mode with Networking to disable EDR and third-party antivirus services before running the encryptor.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.usage: Uses harvested domain credentials (Mimikatz, LSASS dumps) for RDP and SMB lateral movement; frequently escalates to Domain Admin before ransomware detonation.

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.usage: Runs Mimikatz and ProcDump against lsass.exe during the discovery stage; harvested credentials are re-used for SMB and RDP pivoting.

sources.title: UNC4393 Goes Gently into the SilentNight

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.usage: Runs SoftPerfect Network Scanner (netscan.exe) to map SMB, WinRM, RDP and ESXi endpoints before staging encryption.

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
techniques.usage: Uses AdFind and BloodHound to enumerate domain users, groups and trust relationships before privilege escalation.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.usage: Pushes the encryptor across the estate via SMB and admin shares, launched with PsExec or WMI from a compromised jump host.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
techniques.usage: Uses 7-Zip and WinRAR to package data before exfiltration, typically to attacker-controlled storage over Rclone / MEGA.

sources.title: UNC4393 Goes Gently into the SilentNight

techniques.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.usage: Bulk exfil via Rclone to MEGA, Backblaze B2 and attacker-controlled S3 endpoints; also uses temp.sh / anonfiles for smaller drops.

sources.title: UNC4393 Goes Gently into the SilentNight

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.usage: Deletes Volume Shadow Copies with vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet and disables Windows Recovery via bcdedit prior to encryption.

techniques.name: Service Stop
techniques.usage: Stops Windows Backup, SQL Server, Exchange and third-party antivirus services with net stop and PowerShell before encryption to maximise file coverage.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.usage: ChaCha20 file encryption with an RSA-4096-encrypted per-file key, .basta extension; a dedicated ESXi variant targets VMware VMDK, VMX and NVRAM files.

techniques.name: Defacement: Internal Defacement
techniques.usage: Rewrites the desktop wallpaper and drops readme.txt ransom notes in every encrypted directory; leak-site listing on Basta News completes the extortion loop.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.usage: Through August 2023, primary access was Qakbot-laden HTML-smuggling attachments or malicious OneNote / ISO / LNK payloads; post-Duck Hunt the same channel switched to Pikabot, DarkGate and IcedID.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Voice
techniques.usage: Storm-1811 affiliates flood users with legitimate newsletter subscriptions, then vish over Microsoft Teams from lookalike tenants impersonating internal IT help desks.

techniques.name: Establish Accounts: Email Accounts
techniques.usage: Registers Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenants that mimic the target's IT service desk domain in order to place the Teams vishing calls; PRODAFT documented dozens of such tenants across 2024.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.usage: Opportunistic exploitation of ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2024-1709 / CVE-2024-1708) and Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2023-4966, 'Citrix Bleed') for initial footholds through 2023-2024.
